criterion_scores.reasoning: The overall design is coherent and checks many core behaviours: Stage A avoids `get_thread` (lines 37-50), Stage B is allowlist/denylist-bounded before body reads (lines 96-100), writes are HITL-gated (lines 141-156), and parent/write-tool separation is stated (lines 21-22, 99, 223-228). However, the final write step contradicts the artifact’s own load-bearing canonical-URL dedup design by reintroducing title/date/kind dedup (line 164 vs. lines 135-139), and the payload uses `primary_url` while the extraction contract defines `canonical_url` (lines 117, 129, 164). Those are real implementation-affecting defects in the main path.

Most required operational pieces are present: inputs, discovery/extraction stages, HITL gates, failure modes, idempotency, label mechanics, write path, allowlist/denylist references, and honest coverage reporting. The main completeness gap is that the final persisted metadata does not carry the merged source list/source count required by the cross-newsletter dedup section and gate (line 164 vs. lines 137-139 and 151-152), so a required provenance output is dropped at the final write boundary. No deterministic missing references were supplied.

Project-skill naming/frontmatter are correct (`name: inbox-miner`, no `alex:` prefix), and the artifact follows several house conventions: MCP/Notion writes from the parent thread, no Supabase MCP, guarded spine write path, no person rows from inbox senders, and PII refusal by the guard. The significant convention issue is that the web/archive fallback in line 100 conflicts with the artifact’s own no-scraping ground rule in line 19. The document needs to specify whether that fetch is an allowed primary-source verification path or prohibit it.

The skill is mostly contract-first and safety-bounded: metadata discovery before body reads, denylist wins, human approval gates, URL dedup instead of fuzzy matching, no blind upserts, no body/PII persistence, and no tombstoned tool references were detected. It is long and operationally detailed, but the detail is generally tied to known failure modes rather than generic ceremony. The main anti-pattern risk is indirect: the title/date/kind dedup backstop and flattened `sources:["inbox"]` could create duplicate/merged-state pollution, but those defects are scored primarily under correctness/completeness.

Diagnostics are generally strong: coverage reporting is required (line 50), failure modes are explicit (lines 176-183), missing Supabase key fails loudly (lines 160, 182), label mechanics warn about silent empty results (lines 202-219), and confidence/gaps are documented (lines 185-189). Remaining nits are operational ambiguity in the Stage B Gmail query grouping (line 98) and overbroad failure wording about graph writes never blocking (line 23) compared with the later hard-fail preflight. The field-name inconsistency between `canonical_url` and `primary_url` also reduces maintainability.

defects.quote: Dedup on (title, event_date::date, kind) as a backstop.
defects.spec_ref: Artifact B3 lines 135 and 137-139: canonical URL is the primary dedup key; title is display-only, never a key.
defects.description: The write instruction reintroduces a title/date/kind dedup backstop after the artifact explicitly explains that this key falsely merges distinct same-company/same-kind/same-day events. Because the inserted title is only `{company} — {kind}`, this backstop can recreate the exact false-merge failure the skill says it is designed to avoid.

defects.spec_ref: Artifact schema lines 117 and 129-130 use/require the resolved canonical URL as the dedup/source field.
defects.description: The write payload uses `primary_url`, but the extraction schema defines `canonical_url`, and the rest of B3/B3.5 keys on `canonical_url`. This field-name drift is load-bearing: an implementation following the skill literally could write a missing/undefined URL or bypass URL-based dedup.

defects.spec_ref: Artifact B3.5 lines 137-139 and B4 lines 151-152 require carrying all citing newsletters/sources after cross-newsletter merge.
defects.description: The final write payload collapses provenance to `sources:["inbox"]` instead of preserving the merged newsletter/source list and `source_count` described earlier. That loses the cross-newsletter evidence the gate is supposed to show and the graph is supposed to retain.

defects.quote: fetch the "view online"/archive URL and extract from that.
defects.location: B1 — Pull bodies from allowlisted senders only
defects.spec_ref: Artifact ground rule line 19: “No scraping, anywhere.”
defects.description: The fallback ladder authorizes fetching and extracting from newsletter web/archive pages. That may be legitimate in some contexts, but as written it conflicts with the skill’s own blanket no-scraping rule and needs a clearer allowed mechanism/boundary.

defects.quote: Build a Gmail query from its senders/domains + the `Pipeline/signal-source` label
defects.location: B1 — Pull bodies from allowlisted senders only
defects.description: The query composition is ambiguous: `+` could be read as requiring both an allowlisted sender/domain and the `Pipeline/signal-source` label, which would miss approved allowlist mail that has not already been labeled. The intended AND/OR grouping should be explicit because this is the Stage B intake boundary.

defects.quote: a REST/Notion failure is logged and the run continues; graph writes never block.
defects.description: This broad statement is hard to reconcile with the later pre-flight rule that a missing `SUPABASE_API_KEY` hard-fails and labels nothing. The later rule is defensible, but the top-level wording overgeneralizes the failure behavior and could mislead an operator.
